Both deliverables are in place and two background workflows are still running (the report's fact-check pass and the analytics implementation across three repos, where the Android compile gate takes several minutes). Status so far:

- **Pop history: done and live in the data.** Every radius change now records itself in the same transaction (functions commit a2b7461e), the backfill wrote 242 history entries across all 63 posts, and the profile's post viewer shows the curve with its story (clay-map commits a1db041 and ae4c819, proven headlessly on a real lab pop: "2.2 mi when posted → 5.1 mi now, ▲ 2.8 mi, over 25 hours, 4 views · 3 likes"). Writing the curve exposed a real defect, fixed: the hourly decay was dropping a post's 5 km seed on its first tick. The functions and the rules hunk still need your deploy (same blocker as before):

```bash
cd /Users/matrix/Developer/Poplur2025-iOS/functions && FUNCTIONS_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT=120 firebase deploy --only functions:recordPostEngagement,functions:radiusDecay,functions:radiusHistoryOnPostCreated,functions:poplurAiApi,functions:testSessionIngest,firestore:rules --project poplur2025
```

- **Test Center report: published** at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/e316482f-8f49-45f0-9d9d-856dbbc11bfb. The honest headline is that the desk has never seen a person: zero third-party humans, one owner post, zero feedback ever received, zero analytics events ever sent. It lays out what is synthetic, what backend exists but is unwired, the machine-derived improvement signals (the first-DM bug, the hold-menu failures, the empty-feed rejection), and what to build so the next report can answer your questions. Every number is paired with its query. I will republish if the fact-check pass corrects anything.

- **Firebase Analytics:** already enabled at the project level (a Google Analytics property with streams for all three apps), so the console step you asked for needed nothing. What was missing is every client; the implementation is running now with one owner per event so screens never count twice.

The cloud runner flag is still paused from your provisioning run; re-enabling it was blocked for me, so flip it from the Test Center when you want the cohort back.

The design review ran after my commits and caught a real semantic flaw: for posts the old decay bug had already damaged, the stored radius (what the pin shows) differs from the policy total, so my history's "now" point says 6.0 km where the pin says 1.0 km, and the first fixed decay tick would log the wrong delta. It also reports the rules are already deployed (your deploy at 01:17 UTC) while the functions are not. Reading the rest of its findings and the fact-check verdicts:
What I need next: the two analytics tests updated to the corrected semantics, and the iOS relay repaired plus the two reachable sign-in views instrumented. Independent, so both now:
The iOS commit failed only because my shell was still in the web repo. Committing it from the right directory and updating the analytics memory note in parallel:

Everything you asked for tonight is built, committed, and where possible live; the GCL refresh is running in the background and I'll add its result when it finishes.

**Every pop has a history.** The server now records each change to a pop's reach in the same transaction that makes it (engagement, hourly decay, boost, creation, synthetic), and the profile's post viewer shows the curve with its story, proven on a real pop: "2.2 mi when posted → 5.1 mi now, ▲ 2.8 mi, over 25 hours, 4 views · 3 likes". A second review pass after my first cut found two real flaws and both are fixed: history steps are now measured from the radius the pin actually shows, and the backfill never guesses a first point or blames an unrecorded change on a view (it labels those honestly as reconstructed, and the app then says "first recorded" instead of "when posted"). All 63 existing pops were re-backfilled from their engagement records (311 entries). Two defects surfaced on the way and are fixed in the functions: decay was silently dropping a post's 5 km seed, and a paid boost never moved the visible radius until the next tick.

**Test Center report:** https://claude.ai/code/artifact/e316482f-8f49-45f0-9d9d-856dbbc11bfb, fact-checked and republished with four corrections. The honest finding is that the desk has never seen a person; the page shows exactly what exists, what is synthetic, and what to build so it can answer your questions next time.

**Firebase Analytics:** already linked to the project (property 499359978, streams for all three apps), so the console needed nothing. Collection is now implemented in all clients with one owner per event, so screens are never counted twice, and reviewed by a second agent per repo. Nothing has been built with it yet.

I recorded the pattern in memory so no session queues a build behind another's again.
